title: Observation of near-infrared fluorescence from within biological specimens using X-ray light-sheet microscopy for deep-tissue imaging
task: Extend X-ray light-sheet microscopy to near-infrared fluorescence for deeper tissue imaging
key_results: NIR detection achieved 800 μm imaging depth in mouse brain vasculature versus 300 μm for visible light (2.7-fold improvement); Y₂O₃:Yb,Er phosphor identified as optimal rare-earth emitter
comments: The trade-off between reduced scattering (favoring NIR) and steeper depth-dependent attenuation (hindering it) suggests fundamental physical limits that may constrain practical gains beyond the demonstrated 2.7-fold improvement.

model_io.model: MAXWELL (X-ray light-sheet microscopy with NIR detection)

hypotheses.hypothesis: NIR light reduces tissue scattering compared to visible wavelengths, enabling greater imaging depth
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 2.7-fold depth improvement (800 μm vs 300 μm) with less lateral broadening in NIR channel

hypotheses.hypothesis: Y₂O₃:Yb,Er composition produces superior NIR fluorescence signal among rare-earth ceramics
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Screening identified Y₂O₃:Yb,Er as highest camera-detected NIR signal producer

hypotheses.hypothesis: Depth performance is jointly determined by detector response, phosphor brightness, and tissue optical attenuation
hypotheses.result: Supported: Steeper NIR attenuation with depth observed despite reduced scattering, reflecting wavelength-dependent absorption competing with scattering advantage
